title: A `Core\Str` search matches inside one grapheme, so `indexOf` can return a position that does not hold the match.
text: [`find_from`] matches code points and never checks that a match starts and ends on a grapheme boundary, and [`position`] rounds a byte inside a cluster up to the next grapheme. So `indexOf("e\u{301}x", "\u{301}")` returns `1`, the position of `x`; `indexOf("ab\u{1F1E9}\u{1F1EA}", "\u{1F1EA}")` returns `3`, which is the length and holds nothing; and `indexOf` of `"\u{1F1EA}\u{1F1E9}"` in two German flags returns `1`, a match across two flags. A needle that is a whole cluster's leading part, `"e"` in a decomposed `é`, returns `0`, where `Core\Str::slice($s, 0, 1)` is `"é"`. The fix is one of two semantics for the whole search family (`indexOf`, `lastIndexOf`, `contains`, `countOf`, `before`, `after`, `split`, `replace`): matches only on cluster boundaries, as intl's `grapheme_strpos` does, or code-point matches that report a position no cluster rounds. The first diverges from `str_contains` and `str_replace` on decomposed text, the second gives up the rule that every position is a grapheme, so it is a decision on PHP compatibility and not a slice.
